_comment: REGRESSION fixture — what src/script.js does today, through window.__test__. `anchor.*` and `f(Y)@year` are read at J2000; `epoch@tMa.*` re-reads the seven globals AT that epoch (they are meant to depend on it). epoch@0Ma equals anchor.*: resetEpochToJ2000 restores the module-load seeds exactly, so roundTripDrift.* keys never appear. Must never change unintentionally. Regenerate: npm run build && node test/browser/snapshot.test.mjs --write

values.edge.noticeText: The navigable domain ends here, at the Earth–Moon genesis 4,429 Myr ago — the end of the cited Earth–Moon history (Farhat et al. 2022). Nothing is drawn before the Moon exists.
values.domainHover@era: How far the model is validated at this date. Within 500 million years of today every quantity is certified: the gates cover the historical eclipses, the ΔT and length-of-day record, the cardinal points and 45 paleoclimate anchors, and the published API serves this range.
values.domainHover@-400Myr: How far the model is validated at this date. Within 500 million years of today every quantity is certified: the gates cover the historical eclipses, the ΔT and length-of-day record, the cardinal points and 45 paleoclimate anchors, and the published API serves this range.
values.domainHover@-2Gyr: This date lies outside the ±500 Myr certified range. What you see is the model's own extrapolation on cited inputs. Moon distance: the published Earth–Moon history (Farhat et al. 2022). Length of day: derived from it by angular-momentum conservation. Obliquity: a band of possible values, not one value. Precession clock: the composed lunisolar law, not calibrated against any rock record here. Earth map: a generated illustration, continents not modelled. Results are reproducible, not converged.
values.domainHover@edge: The simulator cannot go further back: the published Earth–Moon distance history (Farhat et al. 2022) ends at 4,429 million years ago and the model does not extrapolate it. The Sun is about 140 million years older (4,567 Ma), but nothing is drawn before the Moon exists. Everything shown at this date is reproducible, not converged.
values.domainHover@futureEdge: The simulator cannot go further forward: its precomputed tables end 1,000 million years after today, the range of the charts. The Moon's recession is held at today's measured rate. Beyond ±500 Myr the results are reproducible, not converged.
